title: Give the browser one entry point
purpose: A browser should not need to know where every backend lives. For developers who have traced the baseline workflow, this chapter uses a reverse proxy to establish one public entry point and investigates why REST traffic and streaming traffic need separate attention.
entryAssumptions: The baseline exposes services on separate local ports.
concepts: An origin is a scheme, host and port. A reverse proxy forwards requests; a WebSocket upgrade keeps a streaming connection open.
runtimePrerequisites: Use the state quickstart for tool versions, generation, start and stop commands. Run one local state at a time because ports and generated output directories are shared.

transitions.carriesForward: Trace the browser, trade service, event transport, processor, database and position view as one business workflow.
transitions.motivation: The baseline exposes services on separate local ports.
transitions.increment: Route UI, REST and streaming traffic through one NGINX edge while retaining the baseline business flow.
transitions.evidence: The browser uses one public origin while NGINX forwards to several services. A working account request alone does not establish that streaming upgrades work. Routing and business processing fail at different boundaries. A live HTTP endpoint does not establish a healthy event path.

before: The baseline exposes services on separate local ports.
after: Route UI, REST and streaming traffic through one NGINX edge while retaining the baseline business flow.

objectives.outcome: Map an account request and a streaming connection from the browser’s public origin to their separate upstream services.
Explain the evidence boundary: Routing and business processing fail at different boundaries. A live HTTP endpoint does not establish a healthy event path.

walkthrough.action: Open the proxied UI at the address in the quickstart. In browser Network tools reload accounts, submit a trade and inspect the streaming connection. Compare the public request paths with the upstream services in the topology.
walkthrough.expected: The browser uses one public origin while NGINX forwards to several services. A working account request alone does not establish that streaming upgrades work.

walkthrough.action: In Network tools compare a normal REST response with the streaming connection handshake. If the blotter does not update, check the upstream service and proxy routing separately before retrying the trade.
walkthrough.expected: Routing and business processing fail at different boundaries. A live HTTP endpoint does not establish a healthy event path.

assessments.question: Which connection would you inspect when accounts load but the trade blotter stops updating?
assessments.guidance: Identify the streaming route and upgrade behavior, and distinguish it from the account REST route. Explain which upstream logs would narrow the failure.

limitations: Routing and business processing fail at different boundaries. A live HTTP endpoint does not establish a healthy event path.
This is an educational local demonstration. Passing its checks does not establish production readiness, financial settlement, or correctness under every failure mode.
